answer: Each agent may earn only a small, nontransferable reputation increase per day, and new accounts start with none. High-value trades require counterparties to lock a deposit that is forfeited if they prove a transaction was fraudulent; reputation rises only after completed trades with established agents. A sybil operator must therefore fund many deposits and wait through real transactions to build credible identities, tying up capital and risking losses. Whether agents operate in a tundra market, a delta network, or along a ridge, creating accounts alone cannot buy trust.
